title: What automatic observations do and do not capture
summary: Record tool lifecycle metadata locally when agent hooks (Codex, Claude Code) deliver it; events are labelled codex_hook or claude_hook. Save semantic decisions via the memory CLI; hooks do not understand conversations. Check health each fresh session. Never claim configured hooks are active without live evidence.
body: Raw prompts, command bodies, credentials and tool outputs are not copied into hook events. Tool IDs, timing, explicit exit codes and transcript pointers support investigation. Hosted web tools may be uncovered. This is observation and continuity, not a security sandbox. Local event logs are not Git history; record important outcomes in versioned records and focused commits. Current events are persisted in project-memory/events/ by timestamp and can be read in later agent sessions in the same folder. Claude Code delivery observed live 2026-09-27; Codex delivery still unverified until Codex trusts project hooks. Events are local and not committed; record material findings separately in Git-tracked records.
change_reason: Hooks now cover Claude Code as well as Codex
